novelty_point.claim_en: Proposed a new distributed graph neural network training framework based on graph summarization, called DSGNN, for graph representation learning based on graph neural networks in distributed scenarios.
technical_features: 可以在工作节点上对子图进行小批量样本的学习，而不是让领导节点完成子图生成。
使用图摘要技术生成的子图规模远远小于原图，在其基础上进行模型训练可以大大提升效率。
technical_features_en: Can perform mini-batch sample learning on subgraphs at worker nodes instead of having the leader node complete subgraph generation.
The subgraphs generated using graph summarization technology have a much smaller scale than the original graph, allowing for efficient model training based on them.

work.title: ScaGNN: a Graph Neural Network for Multiple Scattering Simulations

source_record.title: ScaGNN: a Graph Neural Network for Multiple Scattering Simulations
source_record.abstract: The boundary element method (BEM) provides an efficient numerical framework for solving multiple scattering problems in unbounded homogeneous domains. By restricting the discretization to the domain boundaries, it substantially reduces computational complexity. The procedure first consists in determining the solution trace on the boundaries of the domain by solving a boundary integral equation. Then, the volumetric solution can be recovered at low computational cost using a boundary integral representation. As the first step of the BEM represents the main computational bottleneck, we present ScaGNN, a learning-based approach designed to approximate the solution trace. It relies on a graph neural network architecture that incorporates a dynamic adaptive edge sampling mechanism for selecting the most relevant interactions to model. Guided by intermediate predictions of expected error and edge length, this mechanism selects, at various stages of the forward pass, the most relevant distant interactions to model. The proposed method is tailored to achieve linear complexity with the number of nodes in the input graph. To train and evaluate our network, we present a benchmark consisting of several datasets with different types of multiple scattering problems. Our experiments show that our approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art learning-based methods on the considered tasks and investigate the generalization capabilities to settings with an increased number of obstacles and out-of-distribution obstacle shapes. github.com/LARIAD/ScaGNN
